documents.title: Leaf Blight in Maize
documents.content_en: Maize leaf blight commonly appears as elongated tan or brown lesions on leaves and spreads faster in warm, humid conditions. Remove badly affected crop residue after harvest, avoid overhead irrigation where possible, keep balanced nutrition, and consult the local KVK or agriculture officer for a labelled fungicide when lesions are spreading quickly.

documents.title: Common Rust in Maize
documents.content_en: Common rust in maize forms small reddish-brown pustules on both sides of the leaf. It usually needs close monitoring first; if many leaves are affected before grain filling, farmers should contact an agriculture officer for locally approved fungicide guidance. Resistant hybrids and clean field sanitation reduce repeat risk.

documents.title: Rice Blast
documents.content_en: Rice blast causes spindle-shaped leaf spots with grey centres and brown margins, and can also affect the neck of the panicle. High humidity, dense planting, and excess nitrogen increase risk. Avoid heavy single nitrogen doses, keep proper spacing, drain excess water when advised locally, and use locally recommended fungicide only after confirming symptoms.

documents.title: Brown Spot in Rice
documents.content_en: Rice brown spot appears as oval brown lesions and is often worse where crop nutrition or soil health is weak. Improve balanced fertilization based on soil testing, avoid plant stress, use quality seed in future seasons, and monitor the field after wet or humid weather.
